About sources, numbering and grading

Wording, translation, numbering and grading differ between collections and editions, so check the original source before relying on any narration.

Text read inside QORA comes from an open Hadith dataset (fawazahmed0, served through jsDelivr). Gradings appear only when that dataset supplies them, and QORA adds none of its own.

These are important collections, not every Hadith ever recorded. A collection’s name is never proof that a report is authentic.

EDITORIAL STANDARDS

Trust is built into the process.

Source is not commentary

Canonical source text, translation, tafsir/commentary, Hadith, grading, scientific evidence, and AI explanation must be visually distinguished.

Rights are edition-specific

Free to view does not automatically mean permission to copy, host, modify, download, or sell. Record the exact license for each item.

Do not invent a citation

If evidence is missing, say: “I couldn’t verify this in the available sources.” AI output is not an authenticated religious ruling.

QORA is a study aid. For religious rulings, please consult qualified scholars.

NAMAZ · PRAYER TIMES

Prayer times

Choose your location to see accurate prayer times.

Next prayer — --

    Offline city list

    Today

      Next 7 days

      Choose a location to see the week.

      Accuracy & local masjid match

      Match your local masjid

      Enter the time your masjid or local timetable shows and QORA works out the minute offset for you. You can also type the offset directly (−60 to +60).

      Cross-check with an independent source

      Compares today’s times with the free AlAdhan calculator using the same coordinates and method. Only your coordinates, date and method are sent, and only when you press the button.

      Within about 10 km the calculated times differ by only a few seconds, so most differences between apps come from the method, the school (Asr) and rounding, not from distance. A local masjid may also follow its own fixed timetable, which is what the offsets are for.

      School of thought & method

      Leave elevation at 0 unless you have a clear, flat horizon (sea, open plain, a summit). The correction moves sunrise earlier and Maghrib later in the wrong direction for valleys and hill towns, where mountains hide the sun sooner. The detected elevation of a place is shown for information only and is never applied automatically.

      Alerts & alarms

      Web pages cannot ring while closed. For alarms that work with the app closed, add the calendar alarms: your phone calendar will notify you.

      Qibla & Hijri date

      Choose a location to see the Qibla direction.

      Custom coordinates

      For a spot that search cannot find, enter coordinates (for example copied from a map app).

      Prayer times are calculated on your device from the sun’s position, so they keep working offline. Searching for a place, naming a GPS fix and the optional cross-check contact free third-party services (Open-Meteo, BigDataCloud and AlAdhan) and send only the text you search for or the coordinates you choose. Methods differ between scholars and regions, so check against your local masjid or Islamic centre timetable and use the minute offsets if needed. Near the poles, high-latitude rules apply.

      OPEN LIBRARY · EDITOR’S PICKS

      Free books worth your time.

      A curated starter shelf for cosmology, astronomy, Islamic intellectual history, and careful conversations about religion and science. “Recommended” means selected for provenance, educational value, or open access—not fabricated star ratings.

      Read access versus reuse. A free website or PDF is not always free to re-host, modify, translate, or sell. Each card shows what kind of access it offers. Historic public-domain books are valuable for history, but they are not substitutes for modern science textbooks; copyright can also vary by country.

      How QORA recommends reading

      1. Start with a modern, reviewed science textbook for current scientific claims.
      2. Use university/encyclopedia articles for historical framing.
      3. Read Qur’anic text and translation as distinct sources; consult tafsir and qualified scholarship for interpretation.
      4. Separate established scientific findings from interpretive connections, disputed readings and speculation.
      5. When recommending a book publicly, display edition, author, access mode, license and date checked.

      Find more open books

      These catalogues index many more free works. Access and license must be checked for each individual title.

      QORA is founded, designed and built by Zeeyan Rashed, with one aim: a calm, trustworthy place to read the Qur’an, learn and discover, with every source in plain view.

      PRODUCT PRINCIPLES

      Accuracy over appearance.

      Evidence is visible

      Source text, translation, commentary, report grading, scientific evidence and generated explanation stay distinct.

      Rights are checked

      Open access, permission to host, permission to alter, and permission to monetize are different questions.

      Uncertainty is explicit

      If a claim cannot be verified from the available source records, QORA says so.

      PRIVACY NOTICE

      How QORA handles your data.

      Version 2026-10-25. A plain-language description of how QORA handles your data.

      If you use QORA as a guest

      Bookmarks, notes, drafts, quiz progress, reading position, preferences and AI chat history are saved in your browser’s storage on your device. They are not sent to QORA unless you turn on sync. This storage is not encrypted and can be read by anyone using the same browser profile. Clearing browser data removes it. You can export or erase it in Settings.

      If you sign in with Google

      QORA uses Supabase to run accounts, with Google as the sign-in provider. From Google we receive your name, email address, profile-picture link and a Google account identifier. We never see your Google password. Supabase also records account and sign-in times and technical details such as IP address and browser, which are used to keep accounts secure. We store the date and version of the Terms and Privacy Policy you accepted on your account. Your browser keeps a sign-in token so you stay signed in until you sign out; “Sign out on all devices” ends every session.

      Optional online features

      Cross-device sync and publication applications send the data you choose (for example drafts, saved items, manuscripts and contact email) to QORA’s Supabase database, protected by row-level security so that other users cannot read your private records. Nothing is uploaded for sync until you switch it on.

      Other services your browser may contact

      Content features load data from third-party sources such as AlQuran.cloud, the Islamic Network CDN, HadeethEnc, Crossref, OpenAlex, Europe PMC, Open Library and Wikipedia, which receive your IP address and the request. If you search for a place or use your location in Prayer times, Open-Meteo and BigDataCloud receive the text you searched or the coordinates you chose, and AlAdhan receives your coordinates if you press the cross-check button; each also receives your IP address. Supabase is hosted in Asia-Pacific (Singapore), so account data is processed outside your country. If you paste your own AI provider key, your questions go directly from your browser to that provider under its own terms. Do not enter passwords or sensitive personal details into AI tools.

      Cookies and similar storage

      QORA stores settings, reading progress, notes and drafts in your browser for the features you use. QORA displays advertising through Google AdSense; Google and its advertising partners may use cookies or similar technologies to serve, personalise and measure ads, under Google’s own policies. You can manage ad personalisation at adssettings.google.com or learn how Google uses data at policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites. Google and Supabase may also set their own cookies on their own domains while you sign in. QORA does not run its own analytics trackers.

      Your choices and rights

      You can sign out at any time, export or clear local data in Settings, and withdraw by not using optional features. To access, correct or delete data held in your online account, use the Contact page; depending on where you live, you may have additional legal rights. Account sign-in is intended for people old enough to hold a Google account in their country.

      TERMS

      Terms of use.

      By using QORA you agree to these terms. They may be updated as QORA grows; the version date is shown below.

      Source and educational limitations

      QORA may contain incomplete records. It must not be used as an authoritative religious source, legal, medical or scientific opinion, or as proof that any item is licensed for redistribution.

      Contributor rights

      Contributors must have the right to share what they submit. QORA may decline or remove submissions, and handles correction and takedown requests through the Copyright & corrections page.

      Accounts

      You may sign in with Google or use QORA as a guest. By creating an account or signing in you confirm that you accept these Terms and the Privacy Policy; the date and version are recorded on your account. You are responsible for activity on your account and for keeping your Google account secure. Do not misuse QORA, attempt to access other people’s data, or submit content you do not have the right to share.

      Availability

      QORA is provided as is. Much of your data is stored only in your browser, and there is no guarantee of backup, uninterrupted availability, or any particular publishing outcome. Export important work from Settings. Version 2026-10-25.
